files.purpose: SwiftUI view for the Settings > Models page: a "Your models" section listing the pinned models (AppSettings.modelList, at most AppSettings.modelListLimit) with a drag grip for reordering, a click-to-open EffortSliderCard popover (330 wide, trailing arrow) for per-model reasoning effort and fast mode, and a minus button to unpin; then one collapsible section per available provider whose eager card walks the whole catalogue and reveals rows by search, expansion and pin state, each with an add/remove control that is disabled at 0.35 once the picker is full. It also owns the search matching rule (short name, name, detail, raw id, provider display name, localized case-insensitive) and, new at B3, declares the non-private CollapsibleProviderHeader disclosure header that both this page (subject "model list") and SettingsView.swift:647 (subject "provider settings") use.

feature_notes: SOURCE FACT: Grip cursor mechanism rewritten. B2 pushed NSCursor.closedHand in dragChanged on a new drag (B2 :120) and popped in dragEnded (B2 :139); the grip pushed NSCursor.openHand on hover (suppressed while dragged), popped on leave, on disappear while hovered, and on drag release away from the grip (B2 :185-199). B3 removes all NSCursor calls from this file: the grip's onHover now only sets isHoveringGrip (:183) and the cursor is the declarative `.pointerStyle(isDragged ? .grabActive : .grabIdle)` (:184). The doc on isHoveringGrip changed from "for the grab cursor" to "which brightens its icon" (:170). Consequence for the spec: PR-SETTINGS-186's cursor text (push/pop, three balancing guards, Windows path 'balance every push with a pop') describes behaviour that no longer exists; the cursor is now a per-view style keyed on isDragged, with no global cursor stack and so no stranded-cursor failure mode.

SOURCE FACT: The provider disclosure header (B2 :341-364, inline in ProviderModelsSection) was extracted into a new non-private `struct CollapsibleProviderHeader` (:415-448) taking `subject`; ProviderModelsSection now calls it with subject "model list" (:326) and SettingsView.swift:647 calls it with subject "provider settings". Help, a11y value, hint and header trait are the same strings as B2 for this page ("Hide the model list" / "Show the model list" / "Shows or hides the model list"), now built by interpolation `"Hide the \(subject)"`. No observable change on the Models page; ChromeQuietButtonStyle now has a single use site (ModelsSettingsPage.swift:440) serving both pages.

SOURCE FACT: The same grabIdle/grabActive pattern appears at B3 in FollowUpQueueTab.swift:384 and a grabActive-only variant in SidebarView.swift:124, so a Windows grab/grabbing cursor adaptation should be shared across those units.
unresolved_questions: UNRESOLVED: Whether SwiftUI keeps the .grabActive pointer style while a DragGesture is active and the pointer has left the 24x24 grip frame (the row only follows vertically). B2's pushed closedHand persisted anywhere until dragEnded; the B3 source does not say, and it is framework behaviour not visible in the pinned tree.

UNRESOLVED: Windows has no stock open-hand/closed-hand cursor (Avalonia StandardCursorType.Hand is the pointing-hand link cursor). The port needs a platform-adaptation decision (custom cursor resources or an owner-approved substitute) for .grabIdle/.grabActive, shared with FollowUpQueueTab and SidebarView.
